messages:
maya (docs): Heads-up: opened a docs PR to add an "air-gapped time sync & HSM clock" preflight + troubleshooting appendix for Private installs. This came from a customer ticket where PKCS#11 operations failed after a day due to clock drift. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/docs/pull/5014
rajeev (eng-install): Nice — critical. Can you paste the recommended chrony/systemd snippets here? We should match what our installer does for HA nodes.
emma (infra): Also include a short note about VM host vs guest clocks. On some clouds the hypervisor freezes the guest clock; recommend `chronyd` with `makestep` config for big skews.
maya (docs): Draft chrony config snippet in PR: ```ini
# /etc/chrony/chrony.conf (example for air-gapped with local NTP server)
pool 127.127.1.0 iburst minpoll 4 maxpoll 6  # local reference (fudge)
refclock PHC /dev/ptp0 poll 3 iburst  # optional: PTP/hardware clock if available
makestep 1.0 -1
rtcsync
allow 10.0.0.0/24  # restrict to local VPC
```
maya (docs): And a one-liner to check time skew on KMS/HSM host: ```bash
# show drift vs upstream
chronyc tracking; chronyc sources -v
# quick check against sync host
python3 -c "import subprocess; print(subprocess.check_output(['ntpdate','-q','sync-host.local']))"
```
hugo (security): Please add explicit language that HSM appliances can reject signatures with even small skews (often 1-2s). Recommend customers pin max allowed skew in HSM policy and check firmware docs. Also add an openssl time check for cert validity windows when debugging (`openssl x509 -in cert.pem -noout -dates`).
tess (support): From support tickets: include the common troubleshooting steps we send: 1) verify host clock, 2) verify container time (some runtimes don't sync by default), 3) check HSM appliance time, 4) restart KMS daemon after clock fix, 5) re-run key import. Short script snippet we use: ```bash
# support helper: sync host and restart kms-agent
sudo chronyc makestep || sudo systemctl restart chronyd
sudo systemctl restart redwood-kms-agent
# verify agent logs for PKCS11 errors
journalctl -u redwood-kms-agent -n 200 | grep -i pkcs11
```
emma (infra): For container runtimes: note that some minimal containers lack ntp/chrony. Recommend mounting /etc/localtime and /etc/timezone into containers or using a sidecar that keeps time. For systemd-nspawn or chroot cases, mention `timedatectl` might not reflect container drift.
rajeev (eng-install): Installer note: we'll add a preflight that checks `timedatectl show -p NTPSynchronized --value` and verifies skew against `sync-host` using `ntpdate -q`. If skew > 2s, fail the preflight with a clear actionable message.
maya (docs): I'll add a preflight snippet and the exact error message we should surface: "time skew > 2s vs sync host — synchronize clocks and retry installer." Also will include guidance for air-gapped sync hosts: if they are downstream of a lab NTP, recommend using `chrony` with local `rtcfile` or PTP sync for accurate HSM use.
hugo (security): Add a blurb to recommend recording the time sync method in the customer's compliance logs (chrony conf snapshot + `hwclock --show`) for audits.
tess (support): Could we also include a one-liner to detect if the HSM is returning time-related PKCS11 errors? Example grep: `grep -iE "time|skew|certificate|not yet valid|expired" /var/log/redwood/kms-agent.log`
maya (docs): Will add that grep and the suggested wording. CI-bot: PR #5014 lint: markdown warnings, link-checker: no broken links, spellcheck: passed.
rajeev (eng-install): Quick technical nit: for systems using `systemd-timesyncd`, show the systemd unit check and `timedatectl` output example instead of chrony.
emma (infra): Also include Windows Server guidance for on-prem VMware hosts (some customers have mixed fleets). Suggest using `w32time` + group policy notes.
maya (docs): Good call — I'll add a short Windows section with `w32tm /query /status` and a note that HSM drivers may require consistent system time across cluster nodes.
hugo (security): Final ask: include the recommended max skew (2s) and the rationale (HSM firmware tolerance, TLS mutual auth windows). Also link to our internal HSM vendor note (internal link).
maya (docs): Thanks all — I'll update the PR with the preflight snippet, support script, and platform-specific notes. Please review when CI finishes; merging after one approval from eng-install and security. :white_check_mark:
